topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's themes on cancer transformation and genetics, connecting them to prior practicals and outlining the learning objectives.

topics.label: Tumour viruses and the identification of transforming genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transmissible tumour viruses led to the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes and the experimental assays used to measure cellular transformation.

topics.label: Classification and mechanisms of oncogenes and tumour suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the functional definitions and genetic mechanisms of oncogenes and tumour suppressor genes, illustrating their effects through cell cycle control and dominant-negative mutations.

topics.label: Sources and mechanisms of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how defects in DNA repair pathways, replication fidelity, and chromosome segregation generate sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer.

topics.label: Multi-step tumour progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how sequential mutation accumulation drives tumour evolution in both sporadic cancers and inherited cancer syndromes.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session, suggests supplementary reading, and previews the next lecture topic.
